# ProveIt articles on asymptotic expansions and inverses

This collection vendors **46 articles and 2 reference companions** from [VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt at `a9e9c597c2a355702dfe775766ba2c0601653840`](https://github.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/tree/a9e9c597c2a355702dfe775766ba2c0601653840/Analysis/FabiusFunction/docs). The source directory is `Analysis/FabiusFunction/docs/`. Compilation and layout repairs found during this audit were made upstream, with regenerated PDFs committed there before the final vendor refresh.

The selection covers ordinary and all-orders asymptotics, logarithmic and exponential transseries, asymptotic inversion, q-analogs, combinatorial sequence interpolations, saddle expansions, and exact terminating correction hierarchies. Archived articles under `docs/archive/` are excluded. The mathematical claims and their stated proof status remain those of the upstream authors; inclusion and PDF compilation are not independent mathematical verification.

## Provenance and reproducibility

- [Selection and source-line evidence](selection.json) records the decision for every standalone TeX root in the inventory, including exclusions.

The initial audit found PDFs that predated their TeX sources and one article without a PDF. Those artifacts were rebuilt from current TeX. The final manifest records the repaired, published upstream snapshot; refresh evidence preserves the earlier build inputs, exact repairs, logs, and output hashes.

Run these commands from the Asymptotic repository root. PDF builds are serial and use three LaTeX passes. They use a short temporary mirror to avoid Windows path-length limitations; Git on Windows should have `core.longpaths=true` for the preserved source hierarchy.

The upstream refresh records **42 PDFs regenerated and committed upstream**. The current snapshot preserves **48 current upstream PDFs**, with **0 PDFs requiring a build**. Freshness checks use both the pinned Git history and the source checkout's recorded modification times for the full compile dependency closure. A build receipt is accepted only while its PDF, inputs, and all three pass logs retain their recorded hashes.

## q-analogs and inverse q-functions

1. **Universal inverse machinery**. Start here for branch-aware regular/Puiseux inverses, asymptotic transfer, Lambert balance, and residual certificates. These are not by themselves sequence-specific interpolated inverse results.
   [00_scope_status_and_normalizations.tex:97](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/00_scope_status_and_normalizations.tex#L97), [01_universal_inversion.tex:434](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/01_universal_inversion.tex#L434), [01_universal_inversion.tex:547](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/01_universal_inversion.tex#L547), [01_universal_inversion.tex:932](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/01_universal_inversion.tex#L932)

2. **Fixed and infinite q-Pochhammer near q=0 or finite inverse anchors**. All-order finite-product base inversion at q=0; convergent logarithmic jet at q=1; reciprocal-base inverse at infinity; infinite-product endpoint and central inverse jets. Keep argument inversion and base inversion distinct.
   [02_finite_q_pochhammer.tex:285](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/02_finite_q_pochhammer.tex#L285), [02_finite_q_pochhammer.tex:344](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/02_finite_q_pochhammer.tex#L344), [02_finite_q_pochhammer.tex:547](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/02_finite_q_pochhammer.tex#L547), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:287](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L287), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:463](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L463)

3. **Fixed-argument q→1 product expansion and inverse**. Uniform all-order expansion for q=exp(-t), fixed |a|≤rho<1, closed subsectors Re t>0. Leading -Li_2(a)/t, logarithmic constant, Bernoulli/polylogarithm odd powers; each finite truncation has a stated uniform remainder. Followed by the base inverse.
   [q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph.tex:941](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph.tex#L941), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:525](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L525)

4. **Coalescing q→1 Pochhammer and fixed-target inverse**. Separate regime a=q^x: all-order Bernoulli-polynomial expansion with Gamma normalization for x in compact subsets Re x>0. Fixed target (a;exp(-epsilon))_infinity=exp(-L) has its own all-order inverse a(epsilon) and recurrence, with five explicit coefficients. This is not obtained by assuming uniformity up to a=1 in the fixed-a theorem.
   [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:619](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L619), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:810](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L810), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:832](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L832)

5. **q-Gamma and other q-special-function inverses**. q-Gamma at q→0 has an exact convergent generalized-power series: rational x yields Puiseux powers and irrational x requires collecting ordered exponent collisions. At q→1 the logarithm has an all-order expansion with the t term and even powers; base inverse through cubic order is displayed for x≠1,2. Also q-digamma, q-beta, q-exponential inverse reductions and finite-order generator with remainder.
   [05_q_special_functions.tex:226](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L226), [05_q_special_functions.tex:279](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L279), [05_q_special_functions.tex:311](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L311), [05_q_special_functions.tex:358](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L358), [05_q_special_functions.tex:375](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L375), [05_q_special_functions.tex:459](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L459), [05_q_special_functions.tex:578](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L578)

6. **Gaussian/q-binomial and multinomial inverses**. Complete finite parameter expansion and inversion at q=1, q=0 inverse, centered palindromic ramification, cyclotomic roots, and reciprocal/large-target inverse. Gaussian Coefficient Calculus adds the distinct fixed-base/fixed-lower-index, fixed-base/both-large, and q=exp(-tau/n) double-scaling regimes; the latter has a uniform all-order logarithmic expansion.
   [04_gaussian_multinomial.tex:105](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/04_gaussian_multinomial.tex#L105), [04_gaussian_multinomial.tex:155](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/04_gaussian_multinomial.tex#L155), [04_gaussian_multinomial.tex:411](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/04_gaussian_multinomial.tex#L411), [04_gaussian_multinomial.tex:533](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/04_gaussian_multinomial.tex#L533), [04_gaussian_multinomial.tex:609](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/04_gaussian_multinomial.tex#L609), [Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3848](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3848), [Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3867](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3867), [Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3942](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3942)

7. **Fixed-q large argument and theta/log-periodic inverse**. A different limit: fixed 0<q<1 and x→infinity. The logarithm of (-x;q)_infinity has a quadratic/linear/log-periodic phase formula with O(1/x); its large-target inverse includes an explicit phase correction.
   [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:399](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L399)

8. **Root-of-unity radial products and inverse branches**. For q=zeta exp(-t), the infinite-Pochhammer chapter proves a finite uniform radial formula -A/t+C-Dt+O(t^2) and base inverse A/X+DA^2/X^3+O(X^-4). Do not label this statement all-order. Distinct cyclotomic blow-up scaling for geometric products has a proved all-order logarithmic expansion and Bell exponentiation, universal analytic-germ specialization to q-Pochhammer, and formal inverse frequency/base series. Formal inverse branches are not automatically certified analytic inverses.
   [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:938](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L938), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:19529](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L19529), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:19996](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L19996), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:20060](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L20060), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:20208](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L20208), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:20314](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L20314), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:20895](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L20895), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:20986](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L20986)

9. **Modular exponentially small corrections and proof boundaries**. Exact modular acceleration expresses the q-product in a dual exponentially small nome, preserving information beyond algebraic orders. The certification chapter explains asymptotic truncation certificates; cyclotomic resurgence with fixed normalization is a separately labeled open frontier.
   [12_limits_reciprocity_and_frontiers.tex:10](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/12_limits_reciprocity_and_frontiers.tex#L10), [07_certification_and_frontiers.tex:336](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/07_certification_and_frontiers.tex#L336), [07_certification_and_frontiers.tex:715](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/07_certification_and_frontiers.tex#L715)

10. **Geometric q-Fabius endpoint and inverse regimes**. Fixed geometric q, endpoint variable→0: periodic endpoint/Lambert analysis and inverse transport. This is distinct from the parameter-boundary Gaussian limit q↑1. The q-frontier synthesis includes both proved endpoint formulas and separately labeled general-q programs.
   [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:3719](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L3719), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:3888](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L3888), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:14378](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L14378), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:17160](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L17160), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:17988](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L17988), [06_cyclotomic_fabius.tex:412](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/06_cyclotomic_fabius.tex#L412)

11. **Geometric q-Fabius all-order Gaussian and quantile limits**. At standardized q↑1, the strongest current theorem is an all-order Edgeworth expansion in every fixed Schwartz seminorm with finite Bernoulli-Bell-Hermite coefficients. The CDF and central Cornish-Fisher inverse are treated with an all-order central quantile expansion. Keep the compact central quantile regime separate from endpoint Lambert and moderate-deviation regimes.
   [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:22816](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L22816), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:23821](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L23821), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:23839](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L23839), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:24305](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L24305), [geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex:24381](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers/geometric_q_fabius_frontiers.tex#L24381)

12. **Combinatorial sequence companion**. Combinatorial Coefficient Calculus proves the leading Bell saddle/Lambert estimate and a de Bruijn logarithmic expansion, plus Catalan asymptotics and general inverse coefficients. Its purported uniform higher-order Moser-Wyman theorem was expressly withdrawn at lines 3658–3674. No Fibonacci-named treatment or interpolated Bell-number inverse was found in these two live coefficient-calculus volumes; use the archive/inverse-collection lane for those specific sequence inverses.
   [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3629](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3629), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3658](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3658), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3677](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3677), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:6020](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L6020), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:10491](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L10491)

## Combinatorial sequences and interpolated inverses

1. **What an inverse of a combinatorial sequence means**. Start with the distinction between a discrete threshold inverse, an inverse of a chosen interpolation, and an asymptotic inverse. Interpolation is part of the data: matching integer samples alone does not determine inverse correction terms.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:38914](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L38914), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:181](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L181), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:236](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L236)

2. **Fibonacci: a real-argument interpolation and its convergent inverse**. The dedicated Fibonacci chapter specifies the interpolation and branches, derives a closed inverse coefficient formula, and organizes the real correction terms into log-periodic sectors. The source states convergence and a truncation error bound; this is a functional inverse of that specified interpolation.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:53973](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L53973), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54032](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54032), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54188](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54188), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54278](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54278), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54351](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54351)

3. **Bell numbers: Lambert saddle and forward all-order expansions**. The main volume gives Bell-number forward saddle expansions and a ranked logarithmic organization. No dedicated inverse of a Bell-number interpolant was located. Nonprincipal complex-saddle sectors are explicitly formal; the coefficient-calculus volume separately withdraws its former refined Moser-Wyman claim while retaining leading and logarithmic results.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54625](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54625), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54657](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54657), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54863](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54863), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3627](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3627), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3658](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3658), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3677](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3677)

4. **Fubini numbers: ordered Bell numbers and a convergent pole transseries**. The exponential generating function produces an exact pole-lattice expansion with oscillatory exponential corrections and certified truncation. This is forward sequence coverage; it should not be presented as a Bell-number interpolation inverse.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54871](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54871), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:54906](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L54906), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:55005](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L55005)

5. **Rooted trees: singularity transfer and asymptotic inversion**. The Butcher-Polya chapter develops the Otter-singularity Puiseux expansion, transfers it to all-order rooted-tree coefficient asymptotics, and constructs an inverse with a Lambert carrier and exponentially small sectors.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:40418](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L40418), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:41017](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L41017), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:41268](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L41268), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:41599](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L41599), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:42058](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L42058)

6. **Partitions: Rademacher sectors and arithmetic inverse transseries**. The partition chapter organizes Rademacher terms into forward arithmetic sectors, then gives the dominant Lambert inverse and its subdominant corrections. It distinguishes the chosen continuous inverse from threshold recovery of the discrete sequence.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:45397](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L45397), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:45729](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L45729), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:46528](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L46528), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:46896](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L46896)

7. **Factorial families: double factorial, multifactorials, swing factorial and subfactorial**. Factorial-scale sequence chapters treat algebraic and exponentially small inverse corrections. Parity branches and the interpolation choice are essential; the swing-factorial sequence is not eventually monotone, so a single unqualified inverse would be misleading.
   [transseries_and_inversion.tex:42818](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L42818), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:42900](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L42900), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:43834](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L43834), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:47925](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L47925), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:48030](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L48030), [transseries_and_inversion.tex:53222](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Transseries_And_Inversion/transseries_and_inversion.tex#L53222)

8. **Catalan and balanced gamma-quotient families**. A common gamma-quotient engine gives forward expansions and all-order inverse corrections for Catalan, Fuss-Catalan, central multinomial and related families. The coefficient-calculus volume supplies an additional explicit Catalan forward expansion.
   [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1002](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1002), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1103](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1103), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1147](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1147), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:10491](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L10491)

9. **Stirling and Eulerian columns**. Fixed columns lead to distinct multiexponential or logarithmic structures. The treatment includes second-kind Stirling numbers and surjections, Eulerian columns, and first-kind Stirling numbers with nested-log inverse corrections; these are not interchangeable asymptotic regimes.
   [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1261](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1261), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1342](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1342), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1435](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1435), [Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:1901](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus/Combinatorial_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L1901)

10. **Moment sequences, involutions and alternating permutations**. Endpoint extraction covers Motzkin, trinomial, Delannoy and Schroder families. Involutions require two saddles and a stretched-exponential inverse with nonbounded drift. Alternating permutations use parity-resolved gamma blocks and exponentially small sectors.
   [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1564](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1564), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:1954](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L1954), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:2182](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L2182), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:2330](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L2330)

11. **Graphs, necklaces, Lyndon words and irreducible polynomials**. Connected labelled graphs have quadratic growth phases with successive exponential layers. Divisor-sum families require arithmetic sectors and explicitly defined finite-cutoff interpolations; the volume also separates these inverses from certified discrete threshold recovery.
   [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:2592](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L2592), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:2770](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L2770), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:2854](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L2854)

12. **q-factorials, Gaussian binomials and finite-field enumeration inverses**. The q-product part covers general linear groups, flags, q-factorials, Gaussian binomials, q-Catalan numbers and classical-group orders. It gives functional inverse corrections and convergent fixed-rank inverse Puiseux series. A q-factorial functional inverse is explicitly distinguished from its reciprocal.
   [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3101](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3101), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3231](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3231), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3310](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3310), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3318](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3318), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3368](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3368), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3605](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3605)

13. **Galois theta inverses and the singular q-to-one crossover**. Galois-number inverses are organized on residue sheets with theta coefficients. The separate q-to-one analysis gives uniform dilogarithmic forward expansions and asymptotic inverse crossover corrections. This is a continuous analytic-base limit, not finite-field orders tending to one; crossover convergence is not claimed.
   [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:3998](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L3998), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:4076](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L4076), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:4093](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L4093), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:4207](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L4207), [Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex:4247](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/series-and-transseries/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses/Combinatorial_Transseries_Inverses.tex#L4247)

14. **Related q coefficient and inverse machinery**. Gaussian Coefficient Calculus separates exact fixed-rank, convergent fixed-base bulk, and uniform Poincare double-scaling expansions. The q-Pochhammer monograph supplies complementary large-target product inverses, q-to-one base inverses and inverse q-special functions; the dedicated q reading list gives the fuller branch-aware route.
   [Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3838](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3838), [Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3908](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3908), [Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex:3942](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/combinatorial-coefficient-calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus/Gaussian_Coefficient_Calculus.tex#L3942), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:396](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L396), [03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex:522](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/03_infinite_q_pochhammer.tex#L522), [05_q_special_functions.tex:211](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/exponents-and-q-series/q_pochhammer_q_binomial_monograph/chapters/05_q_special_functions.tex#L211)

15. **Exact dyadic extraction companions**. These companions explain exact finite-spline and deconvolution identities connected to asymptotic prefix laws and Gaussian-binomial coefficient rows. Their principal recovery statements are exact, including zero remainder; they are not Bell/Fibonacci interpolation inverse articles or generic q-to-one asymptotic claims.
   [Dyadic_Up_Extraction.tex:3291](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/inverse-and-sampling/dyadic-up-extraction/Dyadic_Up_Extraction/Dyadic_Up_Extraction.tex#L3291), [Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex:126](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/inverse-and-sampling/dyadic-up-extraction/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex#L126), [Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex:1452](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/inverse-and-sampling/dyadic-up-extraction/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex#L1452), [Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex:1760](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/inverse-and-sampling/dyadic-up-extraction/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex#L1760), [Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex:2329](docs/semi-formalized-research-frontiers/drafts/inverse-and-sampling/dyadic-up-extraction/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values/Recurrence_Free_Dyadic_Values.tex#L2329)

## Selection boundaries

All 87 standalone TeX roots in the final source inventory were reviewed. The selection excludes 32 archived roots at the user's direction and seven external-paper roots whose content concerns exact identities, arithmetic, construction, or asymptotic bounds without substantive expansion treatment. Included chapter fragments belong to their parent articles and are not counted again. The selection file preserves each exclusion rationale.

The reading lists distinguish fixed-q, q-to-one, coalescing and cyclotomic regimes; formal inverses from analytic inverse theorems; and proved, conditional, conjectural, or withdrawn expansion claims. In particular, a Bell-polynomial coefficient formula is not automatically an asymptotic inverse interpolation of the Bell-number sequence.
